reason: E2 states that alumina acts as a diffusion barrier in oxidative environments, but explicitly notes these oxides are unstable in molten fluoride salts, not molten aluminum. E1 shows Al₂O₃ forms as a corrosion product in molten salt, not as a pre-formed protective scale. Neither passage supports the specific premises about aluminization, controlled oxidation to form a scale, or its efficacy against molten aluminum.
premises: Alumina (Al₂O₃) acts as an effective diffusion barrier against oxidation/corrosion.
Surface aluminization can enrich the near-surface region with aluminum.
Controlled thermal oxidation of an Al-enriched surface can form an alumina scale.
An adherent alumina scale will prevent molten aluminum from reacting with the substrate.
